summary.text: Erika Uyterhoeven is the Democratic candidate for the Massachusetts State Senate, 2nd Middlesex District, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She is a state representative for the 27th Middlesex District, an office she has held since 2021, and she won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary for the Senate seat.

paragraphs.text: Erika Uyterhoeven was born in Boston, Massachusetts.

According to Ballotpedia, she earned a bachelor's degree from Wellesley College in 2010, a master's degree from the University of Toulouse in 2014, and a master's degree from Harvard Business School in 2019.

Her career experience includes work as an antitrust economist, as a national field organizer for the 2016 Bernie Sanders campaign, as head of digital and data for Momentum, and as a trainer and workshop facilitator for the Massachusetts Teachers Association and a trainer for Mass Alliance; she also co-founded Act on Mass.
Uyterhoeven succeeded Denise Provost in the Massachusetts House of Representatives, representing the 27th Middlesex District from 2021.

Her 2025-2026 committee assignments include the House Committee on Federal Funding, Policy and Accountability and the joint committees on Aging and Independence; Bonding, Capital Expenditures, and State Assets; and Racial Equity, Civil Rights, and Inclusion.
In the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary for the open 2nd Middlesex Senate seat, she received 37.0 percent of the vote, ahead of Christine Barber, Burhan Azeem, Matt McLaughlin and Tom Hopcroft.
